items.title: Verstappen takes Red Bull's first pole of 2026 as Hamilton splits the Red Bulls and Ferrari
items.summary: Max Verstappen topped Q1, Q2 and Q3 at Sepang and took pole with 1m35.130s, 0.298s ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Isack Hadjar was third on the road and Kimi Antonelli fourth; Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri and George Russell followed. Formula1.com and The Race both note it is the first non-Mercedes-powered pole of 2026 and that Mercedes had its toughest qualifying of the year despite its upgrade package.
items.why_it_matters: Red Bull went from pole-less to the front row and the Mercedes order is reversed, so the race becomes a test of whether the Saturday gap holds across a long, high-degradation run.

items.title: Three power-unit/penalty drops reshape the Sepang grid
items.summary: Hadjar's third-place time becomes eighth with a five-place drop. Franco Colapinto carries 15 places (five for the Baku collision, ten for new engine components) and Arvid Lindblad a back-of-grid penalty; both skipped a Q2 time. The saved official Starting Grid has Verstappen, Hamilton, Antonelli, Leclerc, Norris, Piastri, Russell and Hadjar in the top eight, with Colapinto and Lindblad 21st and 22nd.
items.why_it_matters: Hadjar, Colapinto and Lindblad will have to pass through the field on a Sepang track where tyre wear matters, and Alonso expects the cars starting behind him to come through.

sources.label: The Race: Malaysia starting grid after three penalties

items.title: Aston Martin and Audi gain; Ferrari says its timing was perfect
items.summary: The Race calls Aston Martin-Honda's performance its best of the season: Alonso starts 12th and Stroll 14th, with Alonso saying the car is unchanged since Budapest and expecting to drop back on Sunday. Bortoleto reached Q3 and starts 10th while Gasly is ninth. Hamilton said Ferrari's timing was perfect and that he expected a third-row result before qualifying.
items.why_it_matters: The midfield order is unusually mixed, and teams are attributing gains to circuit layout and set-up windows rather than a clear step in pace.

items.title: Heat Hazard declared and Formula1.com expects heavy degradation
items.summary: FIA Document 3 declares a Heat Hazard under Article B1.5.10 because the official forecast Heat Index exceeds 31.0 degrees Celsius at some point during the Race. The venue is Sepang, with Sunday's start at 15:00 MYT / 10:00 Tallinn. Formula1.com's strategy guide says rough asphalt and extreme temperatures should bring about three races' worth of degradation in one afternoon after two low-wear races. Pirelli's event poster nominates C2/C3/C4; qualifying had Ferrari and Audi runners on mediums in Q1 while most others used softs.
items.why_it_matters: Tyre life and heat management are likely to decide the strategy; official FIA and Pirelli figures remain on the Tyres and Penalties pages.
